fullPassage: Emotion socialization — learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them — starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations serve as a role model for emotion regulation, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may frustrate adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk. Free play is nature's means of teaching children that they are not helpless. In play, away from adults, children really do have control and can practice asserting it. In free play, children learn to make their own decisions, solve their own problems, create and follow rules, and get along with others as equals rather than as obedient or rebellious subordinates. In active outdoor play, children deliberately dose themselves with moderate amounts of fear and they thereby learn how to control not only their bodies, but also their fear. In social play children learn how to negotiate with others, how to please others, and how to manage and overcome the anger that can arise from conflicts. None of these lessons can be taught through verbal means; they can be learned only through experience, which free play provides. Technologists are always on the lookout for quantifiable metrics. Measurable inputs to a model are their lifeblood, and like a social scientist, a technologist needs to identify concrete measures, or "proxies," for assessing progress. This need for quantifiable proxies produces a bias toward measuring things that are easy to quantify. But simple metrics can take us further away from the important goals we really care about, which may require complicated metrics or be extremely difficult, or perhaps impossible, to reduce to any measure. And when we have imperfect or bad proxies, we can easily fall under the illusion that we are solving for a good end without actually making genuine progress toward a worthy solution. The problem of proxies results in technologists frequently substituting what is measurable for what is meaningful. As the saying goes, "Not everything that counts can be counted, and not everything that can be counted counts." Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be rejected. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to him or her, it may be integrated as part of the original experience. This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often unconscious. That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court. Correlations are powerful because the insights they offer are relatively clear. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses. But our attempts to illuminate things this way only make them cloudier. Correlations exist; we can show them mathematically. We can't easily do the same for causal links. So we would do well to hold off from trying to explain the reason behind the correlations. Much of human thought is designed to screen out information and to sort the rest into a manageable condition. The inflow of data from our senses could create an overwhelming chaos, especially given the enormous amount of information available in culture and society. Out of all the sensory impressions and possible information, it is vital to find a small amount that is most relevant to our individual needs and to organize that into a usable stock of knowledge. Expectancies accomplish some of this work, helping to screen out information that is irrelevant to what is expected, and focusing our attention on clear contradictions. The processes of learning and memory are marked by a steady elimination of information. People notice only a part of the world around them. Then, only a fraction of what they notice gets processed and stored into memory. And only part of what gets committed to memory can be retrieved. Many people look for safety and security in popular thinking. They figure that if a lot of people are doing something, then it must be right. It must be a good idea. If most people accept it, then it probably represents fairness, equality, compassion, and sensitivity, right? Not necessarily. Popular thinking said the earth was the center of the universe, yet Copernicus studied the stars and planets and proved mathematically that the earth and the other planets in our solar system revolved around the sun. Popular thinking said surgery didn't require clean instruments, yet Joseph Lister studied the high death rates in hospitals and introduced antiseptic practices that immediately saved lives. Popular thinking said that women shouldn't have the right to vote, yet people like Emmeline Pankhurst and Susan B. Anthony fought for and won that right. We must always remember there is a huge difference between acceptance and intelligence. People may say that there's safety in numbers, but that's not always true. If you drive down a busy street, you will find many competing businesses, often right next to one another. For example, in most places a consumer in search of a quick meal has many choices, and more fast-food restaurants appear all the time. These competing firms advertise heavily. The temptation is to see advertising as driving up the price of a product without any benefit to the consumer. However, this misconception doesn't account for why firms advertise. In markets where competitors sell slightly differentiated products, advertising enables firms to inform their customers about new products and services. Yes, costs rise, but consumers also gain information to help make purchasing decisions. Consumers also benefit from added variety, and we all get a product that's pretty close to our vision of a perfect good — and no other market structure delivers that outcome. Intuition can be great, but it ought to be hard-earned. Experts, for example, are able to think on their feet because they've invested thousands of hours in learning and practice: their intuition has become data-driven. Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their internalized expertise and evidence-based experience. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are. Most of us, especially when we interact with others on social media, act with expert-like speed and conviction, offering a wide range of opinions on global crises, without the substance of knowledge that supports it. And thanks to AI, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to believing it, our delusions of expertise can be reinforced by our personal filter bubble. We have an interesting tendency to find people more open-minded, rational, and sensible when they think just like us. Electric communication is mainly known in fish. The electric signals are produced in special electric organs. When the signal is discharged the electric organ will be negatively loaded compared to the head and an electric field is created around the fish. A weak electric current is created also in ordinary muscle cells when they contract. In the electric organ the muscle cells are connected in larger chunks, which makes the total current intensity larger than in ordinary muscles. The fish varies the signals by changing the form of the electric field or the frequency of discharging. The system is only working over small distances, about one to two meters. This is an advantage since the species using the signal system often live in large groups with several other species. If many fish send out signals at the same time, the short range decreases the risk of interference.

④ competing causal hypotheses(경쟁하는 인과 가설들): 오렌지색 차 사례처럼 여러 인과 설명이 다투는 상황을 가리키므로 정답이다.

det.tip: 빈칸 문장의 대비어(illusion vs actually)를 이용해 정답의 뉘앙스를 잡아라.

ch: 인간 사고의 상당 부분은 정보를 걸러내도록 설계되어 있다.
사람들은 주변 세계의 대부분을 인식하고 그것을 모두 기억에 저장한다.
감각에서 들어오는 데이터는 압도적인 혼돈을 만들어낼 수 있다.
기대는 예상과 무관한 정보를 걸러내는 데 도움을 준다.

questions.passage: Electric communication is mainly known in fish. The electric signals are produced in special electric organs. When the signal is discharged the electric organ will be negatively loaded compared to the head and an electric field is created around the fish. A weak electric current is created also in ordinary muscle cells when they contract. In the electric organ the muscle cells are connected in larger chunks, which makes the total current intensity larger than in ordinary muscles. The fish varies the signals by changing the form of the electric field or the frequency of discharging. The system is only working over small distances, about one to two meters. This is an advantage since the species using the signal system often live in large groups with several other species. If many fish send out signals at the same time, the short range decreases the risk of interference.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 이 체계는 약 1~2미터의 짧은 거리에서만 작동한다.
det.analysis:
① 'Electric communication is mainly known in fish'와 일치한다.

② 'the muscle cells are connected in larger chunks, which makes the total current intensity larger'와 일치한다.

③ 본문은 'only working over small distances, about one to two meters'라고 했으므로 '수 킬로미터'는 사실 왜곡이다. 정답.

④ 'the short range decreases the risk of interference'와 일치한다.
det.tip: 구체적 수치(1~2미터)는 오답 만들기 좋은 지점이니 대조하라.

ch: 전기 통신은 주로 물고기에게서 알려져 있다.
전기 기관에서는 근육 세포가 더 큰 덩어리로 연결되어 전류 강도가 커진다.
이 신호 체계는 수 킬로미터의 먼 거리에서도 작동한다.
여러 물고기가 동시에 신호를 보낼 때 짧은 도달 범위가 간섭 위험을 줄인다.

questions.passage: Free play is nature's means of teaching children that they are not helpless. In play, away from adults, children really do have control and can practice asserting it. In free play, children learn to make their own decisions, solve their own problems, create and follow rules, and get along with others as equals rather than as obedient or rebellious subordinates. In active outdoor play, children deliberately dose themselves with moderate amounts of fear and they thereby learn how to control not only their bodies, but also their fear. In social play children learn how to negotiate with others, how to please others, and how to manage and overcome the anger that can arise from conflicts. None of these lessons can be taught through verbal means; they can be learned only through experience, which free play provides.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 자유 놀이는 아이들이 스스로 결정하고 사회적 기술을 익히게 하는 역할을 한다.
det.analysis:
① 아이들의 자율성과 사회성 발달에서 자유 놀이의 역할: 결정·규칙 준수·협상·감정 조절을 스스로 배운다는 글 전체와 일치하므로 정답이다.

② 아이들의 야외 활동 중 어른 감독의 중요성: 글은 오히려 'away from adults'를 강조하므로 반대된다.

③ 어린이에 대한 경쟁 게임의 부정적 영향: 글은 자유 놀이의 이점을 다루며 경쟁 게임의 해악을 논하지 않으므로 주제가 아니다.

④ 현대 디지털 사회에서 자유 놀이의 감소: 글은 자유 놀이가 무엇을 가르치는지를 설명할 뿐 감소·쇠퇴를 논하지 않는다.
det.tip: 반복되는 핵심어(learn to, on their own)가 주제의 방향을 가리킨다.

ch: the role of free play in developing children's autonomy and social skills
the importance of adult supervision during children's outdoor activities

questions.passage: Many people look for safety and security in popular thinking. They figure that if a lot of people are doing something, then it must be right. It must be a good idea. If most people accept it, then it probably represents fairness, equality, compassion, and sensitivity, right? Not necessarily. Popular thinking said the earth was the center of the universe, yet Copernicus studied the stars and planets and proved mathematically that the earth and the other planets in our solar system revolved around the sun. Popular thinking said surgery didn't require clean instruments, yet Joseph Lister studied the high death rates in hospitals and introduced antiseptic practices that immediately saved lives. Popular thinking said that women shouldn't have the right to vote, yet people like Emmeline Pankhurst and Susan B. Anthony fought for and won that right. We must always remember there is a huge difference between acceptance and intelligence. People may say that there's safety in numbers, but that's not always true.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 제목으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 대중적 생각이 늘 옳은 것은 아니라는 것이 글의 핵심이다.
det.analysis:
① The Safety of Following the Majority(다수를 따르는 것의 안전함): 글은 '숫자의 안전'이 늘 참은 아니라고 하므로 제목으로 부적절하다.

② Why Popular Opinion Is Not Always Right(대중적 견해가 항상 옳지는 않은 이유): 지동설·소독법·여성 참정권 사례로 대중적 사고의 오류를 보여주므로 정답이다.

③ The Power of Teamwork in Scientific Discovery(과학적 발견에서 협업의 힘): 개인 선구자들의 도전을 다루므로 협업이 주제가 아니다.

④ How Crowds Improve Decision-Making(군중이 의사결정을 개선하는 방법): 글의 논지와 정반대이다.
det.tip: 예시 세 개가 공통으로 반박하는 통념이 곧 제목의 방향이다.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 safety in numbers가 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'safety in numbers'는 다수에 속하면 안전하고 옳다고 느끼는 통념을 뜻한다.
det.analysis:

② 위험이 인원수와 무관하다는 것은 이 표현 자체의 의미가 아니다.

④ 사람들이 '다수에 속하면 안전하다'고 믿는 통념을 가리키는 관용구이므로 정답이다. 글은 이것이 항상 참은 아니라고 반박한다.

questions.passage: Information encountered after an event can influence subsequent remembering. External information can easily integrate into a witness's memory, especially if the event was poorly encoded or the memory is from a distant event, in which case time and forgetting have degraded the original memory. With reduced information available in memory with which to confirm the validity of post-event misinformation, it is less likely that this new information will be rejected. Instead, especially when it fits the witness's current thinking and can be used to create a story that makes sense to <u>him or her</u>, it may be integrated as part of the original experience. This process can be explicit (i.e., the witness knows it is happening), but it is often unconscious. That is, the witness might find himself or herself thinking about the event differently without awareness. Over time, the witness may not even know the source of information that led to the (new) memory. Sources of misinformation in forensic contexts can be encountered anywhere, from discussions with other witnesses to social media searches to multiple interviews with investigators or other legal professionals, and even in court.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 him or her가 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: him or her는 이야기를 이해하는 주체인 '목격자(witness)'를 가리킨다.
det.analysis:
① 목격자: 'create a story that makes sense to him or her'에서 이야기가 말이 되는 대상은 목격자 자신이므로 정답이다.

② 수사관: 뒤 문장에 등장하나 이 대명사의 지칭 대상은 아니다.

③ 다른 목격자: 오정보의 출처로 언급될 뿐 지칭 대상이 아니다.

④ 법률 전문가: 마찬가지로 지칭 대상이 아니다.
det.tip: 인칭대명사는 가장 가까운 주어(주체)를 먼저 후보로 삼아라.

questions.passage: Intuition can be great, but it ought to be hard-earned. Experts, for example, are able to __________ because they've invested thousands of hours in learning and practice: their intuition has become data-driven. Only then are they able to act quickly in accordance with their internalized expertise and evidence-based experience. Yet most people are not experts, though they often think they are. Most of us, especially when we interact with others on social media, act with expert-like speed and conviction, offering a wide range of opinions on global crises, without the substance of knowledge that supports it. And thanks to AI, which ensures that our messages are delivered to an audience more inclined to believing it, our delusions of expertise can be reinforced by our personal filter bubble. We have an interesting tendency to find people more open-minded, rational, and sensible when they think just like us.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 전문가는 축적된 경험 덕분에 즉석에서 판단할 수 있다는 내용이다.
det.analysis:
① rely on pure luck(순전히 운에 의존하다): 전문가는 수천 시간의 학습에 근거하므로 운과 반대된다.

② avoid difficult decisions(어려운 결정을 피하다): 빠르게 행동한다는 흐름과 맞지 않는다.

③ think on their feet(즉석에서 재빨리 판단하다): 내재화된 전문성으로 빠르게 행동한다는 뒤 문장과 연결되므로 정답이다.

④ follow popular opinion(대중적 견해를 따르다): 전문성 기반 판단과 대비되는 개념이다.
det.tip: 빈칸 뒤 'because ...'가 근거를 주면 그와 어울리는 표현을 고른다.

questions.passage: Emotion socialization — learning from other people about emotions and how to deal with them — starts early in life and plays a foundational role for emotion regulation development. Although extra-familial influences, such as peers or media, gain in importance during adolescence, parents remain the primary socialization agents. For example, their own responses to emotional situations __________, increasing the likelihood that their children will show similar reactions in comparable situations. Parental practices at times when their children are faced with emotional challenges also impact emotion regulation development. Whereas direct soothing and directive guidance of what to do are beneficial for younger children, they may frustrate adolescents' autonomy striving. In consequence, adolescents might pull away from, rather than turn toward, their parents in times of emotional crisis, unless parental practices are adjusted. More suitable in adolescence is indirect support of autonomous emotion regulation, such as through interest in, as well as awareness and nonjudgmental acceptance of, adolescents' emotional experiences, and being available when the adolescent wants to talk.

det.analysis: 부모의 반응이 감정 조절의 '역할 모델로 작용한다'는 의미다. 'serve as ~'(~로서 작용·기능하다) 뒤에 a role model을 두고, 대상은 for emotion regulation으로 연결한다. 조건의 단어를 모두 사용해 'serve as a role model for emotion regulation' 순으로 배열한다.

det.tip: 과거 사실 서술문에서는 등위·종속절 동사의 시제를 과거로 통일한다.

questions.passage: Correlations are powerful because __________. These insights are often covered up when we bring causality back into the picture. For instance, a used-car dealer supplied data to statisticians to predict which of the vehicles available for purchase at an auction were likely to have problems. A correlation analysis showed that orange-colored cars were far less likely to have defects. Even as we read this, we already think about why it might be so: Are orange-colored car owners likely to be car enthusiasts and take better care of their vehicles? Or, is it because orange-colored cars are more noticeable on the road and therefore less likely to be in accidents, so they're in better condition when resold? Quickly we are caught in a web of competing causal hypotheses. But our attempts to illuminate things this way only make them cloudier. Correlations exist; we can show them mathematically. We can't easily do the same for causal links. So we would do well to hold off from trying to explain the reason behind the correlations.
